failure_summary.description: The answer identified the right entity but added a location, modifier, or expanded personal name beyond the expected answer granularity.
Declarative clues were answered as true/false instead of resolving the entity or value they describe.
A clipped phrase was treated as a request to list associated categories rather than to supply its context-supported referent.
The response selected a related but incorrect candidate for the snack or war described.

patch.reasoning: The batch shows recurring confusion about non-question clue forms and three answers that are correct only at an unnecessarily expanded level. The edits make the intended retrieval behavior and requested answer granularity more explicit; the two remaining wrong-entity choices appear to be separate candidate-selection errors.

edits.content:
## Interpret Clue-Shaped Prompts
A clipped title or quoted phrase is still an answer-seeking clue: use matching context to supply its named referent or completion, rather than listing kinds of documents associated with the phrase. Treat a declarative clue as entity or value retrieval unless it explicitly asks whether a claim is true or false; resolve demonstratives such as “this” to the requested referent.

## Match Answer Granularity
Give the concise conventional answer at the level requested. Do not add an unnecessary location qualifier, specialized modifier, or expanded personal name when the simpler state, event, or common name answers the clue.
